correctness.rationale: For every \(m\ge2,\ q\ge1\) the polar is the 1-Lipschitz-potential polytope in the intrinsic zero-sum Euclidean space. Active edge normals span exactly when tight edges are connected, yielding precisely nonzero one-signed binary patterns in every clique blade. For k nonzero leaves and signed sum s, squared centered norm is \(k-s^2/(mq+1)\). A maximizing assignment has \(|s|\le q\) (otherwise flip one concordant whole blade); for \(m\ge3\), any zero leaf could be activated with squared-norm gain at least \((m-2)q/(mq+1)>0\); for \(m=2\) the equality \(k=mq,\ s=0\) proves the same. Thus all extremal patterns use full-blade signs, balanced by parity, giving \(R^2=mq-(m\bmod2)q^2/(mq+1)\). Polarity and central symmetry give maximum inball radius \(1/R\) and all tangent facets. Both opposite contact normals annihilate any optimal center. Noncontact vertices have strictly positive slack at the origin, so the affine center set is the annihilator of the contact span. Balanced sign vectors span dimension \(m-1\) (even m) or m (odd m); hence dimensions \(\(m(q-1)\)+1\) or \(m(q-1)\). Exact verifier: 18 cases, 126256 enumerated polar vertices, 5 independently enumerated tight-graph facet cases. All ranges and parity boundaries explicitly covered; no infinite proof inferred from finite checks.

value.rationale: Symmetric edge polytopes of clique bouquets form a natural two-parameter family containing friendship graphs and star graphs, with well-established polyhedral facet questions. The full intrinsic Euclidean inradius and exact closest-facet classification are natural geometric invariants not determined by the existing facet count. The parity effect, independence of tangent-facet number from q, and nonunique-center affine dimensions (with an explicit uniqueness cutoff) are structural information for comparing geometric realizations and inball rigidity. This is not a toy arbitrary slice or an isolated table.
